BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Status of Seller material:** These are the other side's documents. Wherever they describe something as "agreed", "settled", "addressed", "adequate" or "fair and balanced", I have treated that as advocacy, not fact.

---

## Headline points

1. **The package departs from our playbook on almost every item.** The cumulative effect is to push nearly all risk back to the Buyer. Thresholds are 5x our position. Fundamentals are folded into the general regime. Fraud is not carved out. Deemed disclosure is combined with a blanket buyer-knowledge bar. Two material completion items (Bluefen and Riverlark) are left unresolved.
2. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover positions.** The SPA Update says Bluefen is "addressed", but DL §2 says there is no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied. The Update says the funds flow reflects "agreed" mechanics, but DL §5 confirms the AUD 420,000 bonuses are absent from it. We should raise these inconsistencies directly.
3. **Two proposals match our fallbacks numerically: the 20% cap and the 18-month claims period. Neither is cleared.** Both need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. A matching number does not mean a cleared position, particularly when it sits inside a package that is otherwise much worse.
4. **The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago.** Every factual item (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation, bonuses) needs a refresh before we rely on it in either direction.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a conditional fallback available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Assessment:** We must not accept or signal acceptance. The Seller is opening at our fallback, which means conceding it now would leave nothing to trade against the much larger gaps on thresholds, fundamentals and fraud.
- **Push back:** Restate 25% / AUD 6.0m. If the team wants to use the fallback as a trade, seek Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft first, and tie any concession to Seller movement elsewhere.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess only
- **Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Assessment:** There are three departures: a 5x de minimis, a 5x basket, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined, the first AUD 250k of qualifying loss is effectively unrecoverable, and many individual claims fall out entirely. This is one of the most valuable points in the package.
- **Push back:** Reject in full. Insist on AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping (first-dollar) basket.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus a "limitations apply to all Claims" rule
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Assessment:** The 18-month figure is the same "matches a fallback" trap as the cap. The more dangerous element is the sentence that any limitation applies to *all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise*. This is a hidden general-regime override. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general limits by default, and it reverses our requirement that those categories stay separate.
- **Push back:** Restore 24 months. Delete the default-application sentence. Each limitation should apply only to the category it is expressly stated to cover.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties: same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity"
- **Playbook:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Assessment:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity, the Buyer may have paid AUD 24m for nothing. Capping that at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window is unacceptable.
- **Push back:** Reject. Reinstate the separate fundamental regime in full.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Assessment:** As drafted, these clauses would purport to limit the Seller's liability for its own fraud. This is a non-negotiable point. Whether such a limitation would ultimately be enforceable is a separate question from whether we allow it into the document. We don't.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, applying across cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. No member of the deal team has authority to trade this away.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL §1.1–1.2)
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Assessment:** DL §1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room, and §1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Combined with §1.4 (no admission that any consent or remediation is required), this would neutralise most warranties.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete §1.1 and §1.2.
  - Disclosure must be specific, fair, and sufficient to let the Buyer assess the nature and scope of the matter, and must be made against identified warranties.
  - Accept §1.4 only to the extent it does not cut down a specific disclosure.
  - State expressly that disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, the fraud carve-out or the specific indemnities.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Assessment:** The clause is extreme. It covers the Buyer *and its advisers*, and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Stacked on the general disclosure, it gives the Seller a double defence.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply to Seller knowledge only, defined by named individuals after reasonable enquiry. It should never apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts (DL §2, as at 22 Sep):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (roughly 30%). There is a change-control consent under cl 11.2 with conditions in cl 11.3. There is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the conditions are satisfied.
- **Assessment:** The Update's statement that this is "addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure. Treating consent as satisfied "on delivery" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions, and a consent with unmet conditions may not be effective. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer representing about 30% of revenue.
- **Push back:** Make it a condition precedent that an *effective* Bluefen consent is obtained **and** evidence is provided that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery. The Seller should carry a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours. Also ask for the current status, since six weeks have passed.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): about AUD 3.2m, "release to be provided following Completion"
- **Playbook:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Assessment:** DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in the data room. The facility also has change-control (cl 8.1), so Completion itself may trigger it. A vague post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with security over its assets and no enforceable discharge.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter from Riverlark.
  - Pay the payout directly to Riverlark from Completion funds as a debt deduction.
  - Require executed deeds of release and discharge (including register releases) delivered at Completion.
  - Any post-Completion mechanism needs an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither is in place.
  - Use the current payout figure, not the "approximately AUD 3.2m" from September.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses. These are not in the funds flow (DL §5). On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, others) have not been addressed.
- **Assessment:** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means that in practice the Company pays after Completion, which is an undisclosed price leakage. The statement that the funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics" is wrong; nothing is agreed.
- **Push back:** Show the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as a debt-like deduction or Seller-funded. Add an indemnity for any amounts or on-costs not captured. Confirm the on-cost position with payroll and tax advisers.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller itself says this is not bank-verified. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Assessment:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials (and possibly other Ironquay deliverables). We should not assume the AUD 180k is owed, and we should not assume it is paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own or validly use Ironquay deliverables.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: either evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, or settlement from Completion funds with an assignment delivered.
  - Ask for independent verification of the payment status.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. It may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Assessment:** We must not accept the Seller's "not expected to be material" assertion, which has no evidential basis. Equally, we must not overstate it: there is **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified loss, and we should not frame our position as if there were.
- **Push back:**
  - Require preservation of logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, with regular updates to the Buyer before Completion.
  - Require Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - Add a specific warranty or indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sized only once facts emerge.
  - Ask for an update now, since the disclosure is six weeks old.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)
- **Assessment:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course", but its own DL §8 says the disclosure does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The renewals are related and should be read together. Per the playbook, we neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor automatically treat them as Debt or a price deduction.
- **Push back:** Request the contracts and timing, and assess whether they are terminable, prepaid, accrued or out-of-pattern. Reserve the position on classification pending that assessment.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties ("settled under the general regime")
- **Assessment:** These are **open** and not settled. Putting them in the general regime would subject them to the inflated thresholds, cap and 18 months. We should not assume unlimited liability as our ask, and we should not concede that they are resolved.
- **Push back:** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own terms, to be negotiated.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Assessment:** The share register is the Company's own internal record, supplied by the Seller. DL §10 concedes that the Buyer has not verified it. It is not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence: an ASIC extract reconciled to the register, share certificates, the issue and transfer history, confirmation of no encumbrances (PPSR search, Riverlark security), and Seller corporate authority (board resolution or capacity evidence). Title stays a fundamental warranty in any event.

### 16. Lower-priority items (DL §7, §9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation only, with no landlord consent stated. Confirm by reading the clause, diarise the notice, and treat the item as low risk.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** An assignment restriction that does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control limb, then treat as low risk.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Reject**; 25% / AUD 6.0m. Fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **Reject**; AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months + limits apply to all Claims | **Reject**; 24 months; delete the default-application override |
| 4 | Fundamentals / Title | Same as general | **Reject**; 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | Not carved out | **Non-negotiable**; full carve-out from all limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Reject**; specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete**; at most named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | **Reject**; CP for effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met pre-Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Reject**; current payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Reject**; AUD 420k + on-costs as a line item / Seller-funded, plus indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity "adequate" | **Broaden**; preserve SOW3 cure; verify the AUD 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Don't accept**; preserve logs, investigate, updates; no assumed breach |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess**; no automatic Debt or deduction |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Reject**; remain open and in separate categories |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register suffices | **Reject**; independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification / assignment only | Confirm; low risk |

### Next steps
1. **Authority:** Do not table the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks unless Amelia Frost gives prior written authority identifying this draft. Any post-Completion Riverlark mechanism needs her approval as well.
2. **Information requests:** Ask for updated facts on Bluefen consent and the cl 11.3 conditions, the Riverlark payout figure, Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 investigation, bonus on-costs, the Sandbar contracts and independent title evidence. The DL is dated 22 September 2026.
3. **Mark-up:** Return a full Buyer mark-up restoring our playbook positions. Prioritise the fraud carve-out, fundamentals, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge, and the Bluefen and Riverlark completion mechanics.
4. **Cover note:** Point out the internal inconsistencies between the Seller Update and its own Disclosure Letter on Bluefen and the funds flow. Make clear that no position is "agreed" or "settled" until it is confirmed through our authority process.

- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply to Seller knowledge only, defined by named individuals after reasonable enquiry. It should never apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts (DL §2, as at 22 Sep):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (roughly 30%). There is a change-control consent under cl 11.2 with conditions in cl 11.3. There is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the conditions are satisfied.
- **Assessment:** The Update's statement that this is "addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure. Treating consent as satisfied "on delivery" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions, and a consent with unmet conditions may not be effective. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer representing about 30% of revenue.
- **Push back:** Make it a condition precedent that an *effective* Bluefen consent is obtained **and** evidence is provided that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery. The Seller should carry a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours. Also ask for the current status, since six weeks have passed.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): about AUD 3.2m, "release to be provided following Completion"
- **Playbook:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Assessment:** DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in the data room. The facility also has change-control (cl 8.1), so Completion itself may trigger it. A vague post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with security over its assets and no enforceable discharge.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter from Riverlark.
  - Pay the payout directly to Riverlark from Completion funds as a debt deduction.
  - Require executed deeds of release and discharge (including register releases) delivered at Completion.
  - Any post-Completion mechanism needs an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither is in place.
  - Use the current payout figure, not the "approximately AUD 3.2m" from September.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Facts:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses. These are not in the funds flow (DL §5). On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, others) have not been addressed.
- **Assessment:** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means that in practice the Company pays after Completion, which is an undisclosed price leakage. The statement that the funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics" is wrong; nothing is agreed.
- **Push back:** Show the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as a debt-like deduction or Seller-funded. Add an indemnity for any amounts or on-costs not captured. Confirm the on-cost position with payroll and tax advisers.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller itself says this is not bank-verified. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Assessment:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials (and possibly other Ironquay deliverables). We should not assume the AUD 180k is owed, and we should not assume it is paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own or validly use Ironquay deliverables.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: either evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, or settlement from Completion funds with an assignment delivered.
  - Ask for independent verification of the payment status.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. It may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Assessment:** We must not accept the Seller's "not expected to be material" assertion, which has no evidential basis. Equally, we must not overstate it: there is **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified loss, and we should not frame our position as if there were.
- **Push back:**
  - Require preservation of logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, with regular updates to the Buyer before Completion.
  - Require Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - Add a specific warranty or indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sized only once facts emerge.
  - Ask for an update now, since the disclosure is six weeks old.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)
- **Assessment:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course", but its own DL §8 says the disclosure does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The renewals are related and should be read together. Per the playbook, we neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor automatically treat them as Debt or a price deduction.
- **Push back:** Request the contracts and timing, and assess whether they are terminable, prepaid, accrued or out-of-pattern. Reserve the position on classification pending that assessment.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties ("settled under the general regime")
- **Assessment:** These are **open** and not settled. Putting them in the general regime would subject them to the inflated thresholds, cap and 18 months. We should not assume unlimited liability as our ask, and we should not concede that they are resolved.
- **Push back:** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own terms, to be negotiated.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Assessment:** The share register is the Company's own internal record, supplied by the Seller. DL §10 concedes that the Buyer has not verified it. It is not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence: an ASIC extract reconciled to the register, share certificates, the issue and transfer history, confirmation of no encumbrances (PPSR search, Riverlark security), and Seller corporate authority (board resolution or capacity evidence). Title stays a fundamental warranty in any event.

### 16. Lower-priority items (DL §7, §9)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation only, with no landlord consent stated. Confirm by reading the clause, diarise the notice, and treat the item as low risk.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** An assignment restriction that does not appear to be triggered by a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control limb, then treat as low risk.
